A — SYSTEM CONTEXT (READ FIRST, BUILD NOTHING YET)

You are working inside a production Next.js 14 App Router monorepo called Torgima-Execution. This is a live, partially-built execution operating system. You must read the entire codebase before touching a single file.

A.2 — What you are building (The Erector Upgrade)

You are UPGRADING the existing validation system — not replacing it. The Erector adds 9 validation engines, 30 Economic Archetype intelligence, civilization-specific reality scoring, time simulation, goal decomposition, and a multi-screen validation UI that gives every user a complete, personalised picture of what their goal actually requires before a single execution task is generated.
The spec that follows is complete and self-contained. You do not need any external documents. Everything you need is in this prompt.

These laws apply to every file you create or modify in this build. Violating any one of them breaks the system.

READ EVERY FILE BEFORE CHANGING IT. Read prisma/schema.prisma completely before adding tables. Read every existing service file before creating new services. Read every existing API route before creating new routes.

EXTEND, NEVER REPLACE. The existing Validation model gets new fields added. The existing onboarding flow gets new screens inserted. The existing validation API route gets upgraded. Nothing is deleted. No existing field is removed.

BHUDHI NEVER ACTS DIRECTLY. Every Bhudhi call must go through BhudhiTriggerRouter with a registered Zod schema. Every call gets logged to BhudhiLog. Every call has a deterministic fallback. If Bhudhi fails, the system continues with the fallback — it never crashes.

RULE ENGINE OWNS ALL DECISIONS. Bhudhi interprets and generates narratives. The Scoring Engine (Step 9) calculates all 11 scores deterministically without any AI involvement. The Control Engine decides if a blueprint can launch. Bhudhi cannot override scores or launch blueprints.

NEVER GENERATE FAKE DATA. Bhudhi uses real market intelligence from its training data for competitor analysis and industry trends. It must not fabricate specific competitor names without grounding. If uncertain, it returns structured placeholders the user can verify.
ARCHETYPE CONTEXT LOADS BEFORE ANY VALIDATION. No engine runs until the Economic Archetype is resolved from the user's location. All scores are archetype-adjusted.
ALL MUTATIONS GO THROUGH EVENTS. When validation completes, when a path is selected, when a blueprint level is chosen — emit the appropriate event. Never mutate state directly from a screen.
IDEMPOTENCY IS ENFORCED. Every validation run checks idempotency_key against existing ValidationRun records before processing. Duplicate submissions return the existing result.

NO PROMISES, NO GUARANTEES. The Erector shows probability estimates and difficulty projections. No language in any UI copy or Bhudhi output may promise a specific outcome. Use 'probability', 'estimated', 'likely', 'projected'.

EXECUTION LANGUAGE THROUGHOUT. No motivational fluff. No 'Great job!', 'Amazing goal!', 'You've got this!'. Direct operational language only. Example: 'Validation complete. Reality Score: 6.8/10. Adjusted path recommended.' Not: 'Awesome! Your goal looks great!'

SAFE MIGRATION PATTERN. All new database columns on the existing Validation table are nullable. No NOT NULL constraint is added without a default. No existing column is renamed or dropped. The migration is additive only.

Engine 8 — Execution Difficulty Engine + Timing Engine
Two engines run together. Execution Difficulty scores 8 dimensions of how hard this will actually be. Timing analyses whether now is the right moment to launch.
1. Technical Complexity — how much technical skill or infrastructure is required
2. Capital Requirements — how much money is needed before revenue is possible
3. Time to First Revenue — minimum realistic days before first paid customer
4. Sales Complexity — how hard is it to close a customer in this economy
5. Distribution Difficulty — how hard is it to reach the target customer
6. Regulatory Burden — compliance, registration, legal requirements
7. Team Requirements — can one person execute this or is a team required
8. Operational Complexity — day-to-day operational demands after launch
